name: stat
title: Stat
purpose: One number in context: a label that says what it counts, the value in tabular figures, and a line that gives its comparison, its period or its scope.
whenToUse: For a number the reader came to the view for: the time a run took, what it cost, how many tests failed.
For two to four numbers that summarise the table or list directly under them.
With the inline variant where the number sits in a line of text: a toolbar, a summary row, the header of a section.
whenNotToUse: As a row of large standalone numbers at the top of a view. A number with no context line is decoration.
For a number measured against a limit. Use the usage meter.
For several facts about one thing that are not all numbers. Use the key-value list.
For the same number about many things. Use a numeric column in the data table.
For a status. Use a badge.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Label, value and context one above the other. The value is 20px, one size above body text.

variants.name: inline
variants.use: Label, value and context on one line at body size, wrapping when there is no room.

accessibility: Use a div holding three p elements in this order: ds-stat__label, ds-stat__value, ds-stat__context. Read in order they make a sentence: Median run time, 6 min 12 s, 48 seconds faster than last week.
The context line is required. It gives the comparison, the period or what is counted, in words: of 50,000 for this run, 8 to 14 March, 48 seconds faster than last week.
The value carries its unit. A rise or a fall is said in words in the context line, never by colour or an arrow alone.
Several stats sit in a ds-grid or a ds-cluster. Keep to four or fewer, directly above what they summarise.

When there is nothing to count, show 0 and say why in the context line. While the number is worked out, set aria-busy="true" on the stat and put a spinner with role="status" in place of the value and context. If it cannot be read, put a context line with role="alert" that says what to do in place of the value.
When the value updates while the reader watches, announce the change from a role="status" element in the view, not from the stat.
The stat has no controls and needs no script.
